```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4, out.width = "100%")
library(searchnet)
```

SAOM-NK works on `B`, an actor-by-component matrix with one slice per period.
Observed data rarely arrive in that shape. They arrive in long format: one row
per actor, component and period, sometimes with a weight. This vignette goes
from such records to `B`, reads the four {K} dimensions off it, and hands the
result to the estimation layer.

## 1. Long data

The example is synthetic: ten actors, eight components, four periods, and a
numeric weight on each record (an intensity, a count, a share).

```{r data}
set.seed(42)
grid <- expand.grid(actor = sprintf("actor_%02d", 1:10),
                    component = sprintf("comp_%d", 1:8),
                    period = 1:4, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
long <- grid[runif(nrow(grid)) < 0.35, ]
long$weight <- round(rexp(nrow(long), 2), 2)
head(long)
```

## 2. Long data to B

`searchnet_bipartite_from_long()` builds the array. A tie is a summed weight
above `threshold`; with `weight = NULL` any record is a tie. Passing `actors`
fixes the universe, so an actor with no records in a period, or none at all,
keeps a row of zeros and composition is stable across waves. A row of zeros
says the actor was there and held nothing; for an actor that did not yet exist
or had closed, use section 6 instead.

```{r build}
obs <- searchnet_bipartite_from_long(
  long, actor = "actor", component = "component", period = "period",
  weight = "weight", threshold = 0.1,
  actors = sprintf("actor_%02d", 1:11),   # actor_11 never appears
  components = sprintf("comp_%d", 1:8))
obs
dim(obs$B)
```

## 3. {K} readings

`searchnet_k_readings()` returns one row per node and period. The definitions
are those of `system.file("rosetta", "K_DIMENSIONS.md", package = "searchnet")`
and are computed exactly as the simulation engine computes its {K}-4 degrees:

- **Expansiveness** `K_AC`: components an actor holds (row sum of `B`).
- **Popularity** `K_CA`: actors holding a component (column sum).
- **Sociality** `K_AA`: other actors sharing at least one component.
- **Epistasis** `K_CC`: other components co-held with a component.

`K_AA` and `K_CC` exclude the node itself. The weighted forms,
`sociality_strength` and `epistasis_strength`, are reported alongside, and the
accounting identities that tie the four together (total ties; second moment of
one margin equals total strength in the other projection) are checked for every
period.

```{r readings}
k <- searchnet_k_readings(obs)
head(k[k$level == "actor", c("period", "id", "K_AC", "K_AA", "sociality_strength")])
head(k[k$level == "component", c("period", "id", "K_CA", "K_CC", "epistasis_strength")])
```

The `"summary"` attribute gives the per-period totals: density, mean degrees,
mean pairwise Jaccard overlap of portfolios, and `tie_jaccard`, the overlap of
each period's tie set with the one before it. Values that are very low warn
that a SAOM will see too much change between waves.

```{r summary}
s <- attr(k, "summary")
s[, c("period", "ties", "density", "mean_K_AC", "mean_K_AA",
      "mean_K_CA", "mean_K_CC", "tie_jaccard")]
```

## 4. Plot

Mean degree per period, one panel per dimension, in the order of the {K}-4
panel.

```{r plot}
long_means <- rbind(
  data.frame(period = s$period, dimension = "Expansiveness (K_AC)", mean = s$mean_K_AC),
  data.frame(period = s$period, dimension = "Popularity (K_CA)",    mean = s$mean_K_CA),
  data.frame(period = s$period, dimension = "Sociality (K_AA)",     mean = s$mean_K_AA),
  data.frame(period = s$period, dimension = "Epistasis (K_CC)",     mean = s$mean_K_CC))
long_means$dimension <- factor(long_means$dimension, levels = unique(long_means$dimension))
ggplot2::ggplot(long_means, ggplot2::aes(period, mean)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() + ggplot2::geom_point() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ dimension, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Period", y = "Mean degree") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

## 5. Into estimation

`obs` goes straight to `searchnet_coevolve_data()` as the bipartite dependent
network, and `searchnet_k_covariate()` reshapes any reading into the
node-by-period matrix it takes for a varying covariate. A degree of the
dependent network entered this way is a lagged reading of the network itself,
a different estimand from the endogenous effects (`outAct`, `inPop`) that model
the same degree as a mechanism.

```{r coevolve, eval = requireNamespace("RSiena", quietly = TRUE)}
arch <- array(rbinom(8 * 8 * 4, 1, 0.25), dim = c(8, 8, 4))
dat <- searchnet_coevolve_data(
  bipartite = obs, component = arch,
  actor_covars = list(scope = searchnet_k_covariate(k, "K_AC")),
  verbose = FALSE)
class(dat)
```

## 6. Actors who enter or leave

Panels lose actors (a firm closes, a developer stops contributing) and gain
them. Coded as rows of zeros, a closure reads as an actor dropping every tie,
and an entry as an actor building a portfolio from nothing, and the estimator
models both as tie changes. RSiena's alternative is an exogenous composition
change (Huisman and Snijders 2003): an actor is active only while present,
and its arrival and departure are not part of the modeled change.

Give each actor's `entry` and `exit` in the units of the period column.
Fractional times fall within a period: below, `actor_03` closes halfway
between periods 2 and 3, and `actor_10` enters halfway between periods 1
and 2. Their records outside those intervals are removed first, because a
record for an absent actor-period is an error rather than a silent drop.

```{r composition}
long2 <- long[!(long$actor == "actor_03" & long$period > 2) &
              !(long$actor == "actor_10" & long$period < 2), ]
obs2 <- searchnet_bipartite_from_long(
  long2, actor = "actor", component = "component", period = "period",
  weight = "weight", threshold = 0.1,
  exit = c(actor_03 = 2.5), entry = c(actor_10 = 1.5))
obs2
obs2$B["actor_03", 1:3, ]
obs2$composition$intervals[c("actor_03", "actor_10")]
```

Absent actor-waves are `NA` in `B`, the coding `RSiena::sienaDependent()`
expects with a composition change. The intervals are kept in RSiena wave time
(wave 1 is time 1). A `presence` matrix (actor by period, `TRUE` when
observed) is the alternative when only the waves are known, and allows an
actor to leave and return.

The {K} readings skip an absent actor and its ties in that period, so
`n_actors` and `density` refer to the actors present, and `tie_jaccard`
compares only actors present at both waves:

```{r composition-k}
k2 <- searchnet_k_readings(obs2)
attr(k2, "summary")[, c("period", "n_actors", "ties", "density", "tie_jaccard")]
```

`searchnet_composition(obs2)` returns RSiena's composition-change object, and
`searchnet_coevolve_data()` adds it on its own when given `obs2`. With a
composition change, RSiena estimates by unconditional method of moments.

```{r composition-coevolve, eval = requireNamespace("RSiena", quietly = TRUE)}
dat2 <- searchnet_coevolve_data(bipartite = obs2, component = arch,
                                verbose = FALSE)
length(dat2$compositionChange)
```

### What ignoring it costs

`searchnet_recovery(composition = )` plants leavers and joiners in simulated
panels. The run below plants a 20% leaver share per period (M = 30, N = 12,
3 waves, 100 replications, planted rate 5, density -1.5, inPop 0.10) and
estimates the same panels twice: with the composition change, and the naive
way, with leavers coded as rows of zeros. It takes several minutes, so the
results were computed by `tools/make_composition_vignette_data.R` with exactly
this code, with the criterion written before the run, and are loaded here.

```{r composition-recovery-run, eval = FALSE}
design <- list(
  effects_spec = c("density", "inPop"),
  theta_true   = c(rate = 5, density = -1.5, inPop = 0.10),
  M = 30L, N = 12L, waves = 3L, reps = 100L, nbrNodes = 1L, seed = 20261011L,
  n3 = 500L, nsub = 4L, init_density = 0.2,
  composition = list(leave = 0.2, enter = 0),
  criterion = list(max_abs_bias = c(density = 0.10, inPop = 0.03),
                   min_coverage = 0.90, min_converged_share = 0.90))
with_comp <- do.call(searchnet_recovery,
                     c(design, list(estimate_with_composition = TRUE)))
naive     <- do.call(searchnet_recovery,
                     c(design, list(estimate_with_composition = FALSE)))
```

```{r composition-recovery-print}
path <- system.file("extdata", "searchnet_composition_recovery.rds",
                    package = "searchnet")
if (!nzchar(path))  # building from a source tree without an installed copy
  path <- file.path("..", "inst", "extdata",
                    "searchnet_composition_recovery.rds")
stored <- readRDS(path)
stored$with_composition
stored$naive
```

All 100 replications converged in both arms. With the composition change,
the planted values come back within the stated criterion (density bias 0.05,
inPop bias -0.02, every 95% interval covering the planted value), and
those small biases match what the same design gives with no leavers at all
(`vignette("searchnet-recovery")`). Read the naive way, the same panels give a
density estimate about 0.22 lower (paired over replications, Monte Carlo SE
0.01), outside the criterion, and a period-2 rate of 4.1 against the planted
5 with 72% coverage: the leavers' dropped ties inflate change in the period
they leave, and their empty rows dilute it afterwards. The popularity effect
moved little in this design (paired difference -0.007), so a stable focal
estimate under the naive reading is not evidence that the baseline
parameters are right.

These results hold at this design (20% leavers per period, no joiners,
M = 30, N = 12, three waves) and nothing more. Run
`searchnet_recovery(composition = )` at your own design, with and without
`estimate_with_composition`, before choosing how to treat exits.

## 7. A project skeleton

`searchnet_new_analysis("my-analysis")` writes a short, reproducible project
that runs these steps in order on a synthetic example: setup and a version
record, long data to `B`, {K} readings, a moment gate against tolerances fixed
in a pre-registered chunk, a small recovery check, a placebo-gated
counterfactual, and a report that prints every null with its minimum
detectable effect. Replace the data file and keep the gates.
